title: Weekly POC Sync - NexusMed routing & networking results
summary: Weekly check-in for NexusMed POC running Redwood Private in their VPC and on-prem gateway. Reviewed last week's latency/throughput numbers, discussed routing fallback behavior across regions, kernel/quantization upgrade plan, and a flaky egress NAT issue. Action items cover a short benchmark run, secure tunnel checklist, and a security artifact to be shared.
next_steps: Redwood: run deterministic 10k request benchmark w/ prefix caching and share CSV by Tue 12/16
NexusMed: provide sample traffic profile and a small corpus of 50 representative prompts by Fri 12/12
Both: schedule a controlled kernel upgrade test window for 12/18-12/19
Redwood SE to share secure tunnel checklist and updated network diagram
action_items: Priya Desai - run 10k deterministic benchmark, attach latency histo CSV - due 2025-12-16
Samira Khan - send VPC peering flow logs and egress NAT config - due 2025-12-12
Alex Kim - share SOC2 + encryption/KMS summary + internal telemetry export instructions - due 2025-12-13
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Oliver Park (NexusMed CTO), Samira Khan (NexusMed Infra), Diego Ramos (NexusMed Sec), Maya Li (NexusMed ML)

Summary (auto): quick sync on POC progress; latency noise isolated to egress peering in one AZ; plan a small kernel/quantization roll and run a deterministic benchmark.

[00:00:05] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I think we have the usual suspects. um, we'll go through the numbers Priya's pulled, then open floor for network specifics.
[00:00:28] Oliver - NexusMed (CTO): yep all good, thanks Alex. We only have about 45 minutes so let's keep it tight.
[00:00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): ok I'm gonna share the dashboard numbers, I posted a quick link in the chat, but main thing is last week's p50 stable around 60-70ms, p95 around 320 but p99 has the spikes to 1.2s, uh mostly on region-eu-west-2 egress path.
[00:00:58] Samira - NexusMed (Infra): that's the cluster with the new NAT gateway we spun up last week, might be related. We're seeing some tcp re-transmits there.
[00:01:12] Jordan (Redwood SE): just to be clear, the p99 spike correlates with a routing fallback from the pinned dedicated node to a cold instance, so we see kv cache miss + model load.
[00:01:28] Diego - NexusMed (Sec): are those model loads visible in your telemetry? I want to be sure no secret keys/inputs are leaking during failover.
[00:01:39] Priya (Redwood SE): yeah telemetry shows a cache miss event and then a call to model-v2 which is in the same VPC; nothing in traces indicate payload escape. our tracing is sampled but we'll attach the trace snippets.
[00:01:56] Oliver: cool, please attach.

[00:02:18] Alex: quick aside—there was a small mis-comm earlier, NexusMed asked about an on prem gateway for low-latency devices at the edge, do we have any updated guidance?
[00:02:32] Priya: on prem is fine, the only caveat is kernel version and CUDA driver parity. for quantized runs we prefer the 535.x series, but we can run on older drivers with fallback kernels. sometimes those fallbacks add about 50 to 120ms depending on sequence length.
[00:02:56] Samira: ok that matches our ops notes. the weird bit is that one node in eu-west-2 will intermittently drop the established connection to the peering VPC; we see bgp flaps — but honestly might be the cloud provider.
[00:03:15] Priya: if it's BGP, that would explain sudden routing switch and then the cold start. We recommend a sticky route for sessions and a short TTL caching at the infra layer, plus Redwood side we'll implement a 2s grace window to keep KV cache alive during transient route changes.
[00:03:36] Oliver: 2 seconds grace window sounds reasonable. how does that interact with memory usage on the host?
[00:03:45] Jordan: it's negligible if we keep it per-request small; the grace lives only in the runtime's ephemeral LRU. we measured mem increase ~150MB on the GPU worker for our 13B-like footprints.

[00:04:12] Alex: moving on to the kernel upgrade plan — Priya you had suggested a canary approach?
[00:04:18] Priya: yes, propose 10% of traffic to kernel-v2 (the new quantized kernels) behind a header flag for 24 hours. if latency/regression looks ok, expand to 50% then full. we need NexusMed to pick a 2-hour maintenance window where you can tolerate a small number of 500s.
[00:04:40] Samira: 2 hours maintenance? prefer overnight during the 02:00-04:00 UTC window. we'll mark it tentative for 12/18.
[00:04:52] Diego: security asks that we get a signed runbook before any kernel flip. includes rollback steps and who to call.
[00:04:59] Alex: we'll put together a runbook, include the auto-rollback threshold and a manual cancel.

[00:05:20] [00:05:20] Priya: okay numbers deep dive — I pulled a 6-hour slice around the p99 spikes. you can see the majority line up with NAT egress retries. also a handful are internal cache eviction windows, probably from our default 45s prefix cache if there's a lot of unique prefixes.
[00:05:42] Maya - NexusMed (ML): are the cache evictions from many users hitting different prompts or is it a few heavy users?
[00:05:50] Priya: the sampling says it's high-cardinality prompts — many different long-tail prompts. recommended: enable prefix aggregation in the agent for a subset of routes, that reduces the cache key cardinality by ~60% in our tests.
[00:06:06] Samira: how invasive is prefix aggregation to our existing routing?
[00:06:11] Jordan: minimal; it's a layer in the Redwood agent config. we can ship a patch that is opt-in per-route. we suggest starting with your internal inference route first.

[00:06:40] [00:06:40] Oliver: on the egress NAT issue — we ran packet captures and saw intermittent icmp unreachable from the NAT device. could be cloud provider scheduled maintenance. any suggestion on fallback routing?
[00:06:57] Priya: implement multi-path fallback: prefer primary route, but if health-checks fail in 200ms, route to the second AZ with sticky session header and allow up to 500ms additional latency. Also Redwood can do in-flight reroute to a warm standby instance to avoid KV cold misses.
[00:07:18] Samira: do you have an example health check config?
[00:07:22] Priya: yes I'll paste an example in the shared doc, it's basically a lightweight /healthz with a 100ms timeout and 50ms interval for 3 failures.

[00:07:48] Diego: related to security — if we route to another AZ, what about data residency? are logs still kept in our VPC?
[00:07:57] Alex: all request payloads stay within your VPC in this deployment. err, just to clarify, Redwood Private control-plane sits in our tenancy but data path is in your network and logs can be pushed to your S3 bucket or retained per your retention policy.
[00:08:14] Diego: ok want that in writing (SOC2 artifact).

[00:08:30] [00:08:30] Priya: quick note on quantization — we saw a 1.8x token/s improvement on 8-bit runs for your typical prompt lengths, but some hallucination patterns changed slightly; our recommend is to run your eval suite before switching default.
[00:08:48] Maya: we have an eval harness of 2k prompts, can we flag a subset as quality-sensitive?
[00:08:55] Priya: absolutely, share the harness and we'll run the quantized variant against it and return BLEU/lang-metric diffs.

[00:09:12] [00:09:12] Jordan: small transcription noise — the Red wood private agent sometimes shows as "Redwood privé" in trace names; ignore that it's just a locale artifact in the agent.

[00:09:28] Oliver: any updates on the secure tunnel? last week you mentioned a hybrid TLS-forwarded tunnel plus mutual TLS for control plane.
[00:09:39] Alex: yes, we have a checklist. main items: mutual TLS with client certs for control plane, optional site-to-site VPN for data-plane, HSM/KMS integration for keys, and audit/export hooks.
[00:09:55] Samira: we prefer VPN + private peering rather than opening public egress. Is that supported?
[00:10:01] Priya: yes supported — we've done a few vibe like that. we usually recommend private peering + explicit egress routes. if you want a fully on-prem air-gapped setup that's a separate package.

[00:10:22] [00:10:22] Diego: can you send the KMS integration doc? we run Vault and AWS KMS for different environments.
[00:10:28] Alex: will do. I'll attach the doc to the CRM and to the channel.

[00:10:45] [00:10:45] Priya: quick note — the telemetry shows a small memory bump after the quant kernel enabled on one host, we need to watch for OOM on smaller instance types. recommend 2x headroom.
[00:11:02] Samira: which instance types are you using in your recommendation?
[00:11:05] Jordan: for 13B-ish models we recommend A100-like or H100 mixed with 80GB variants; for cost-sensitive we test on 80GB A100 with multi-instance sharing — but again memory headroom is king.

[00:11:30] [00:11:30] Priya: ok actionables — I'll run the deterministic 10k request bench with prefix aggregation toggled on/off and attach CSVs and histograms. Also we'll provide the test harness commands so your infra can reproduce locally.
[00:11:48] Maya: can you include seed prompts and exact docker image tags so we can reproduce in our staging?
[00:11:53] Priya: yes, I'll include image tags and the exact kernel sha.

[00:12:10] [00:12:10] Oliver: last thing — on the billing front we wanted a scoped estimate if we move to dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted bursts for the pilot.
[00:12:21] Alex: we have an estimator sheet, will send a scoped delta for reserved capacity vs bursty hosted, plus per-token delta for quantized vs full precision. expect that by EOD Monday.
[00:12:33] Samira: ok thanks.

[00:12:45] [00:12:45] Diego: one more sec — security wants a signed AFA (access framework agreement) before the kernel switch.
[00:12:53] Alex: we'll route a runbook + AFA to legal.

[00:13:10] Priya: small gotcha we found — if you have very high prefix cardinality and also very short session TTL, the backend's cache churn can cause synchronous model reloads; solution is a combination of prefix aggregation and a slightly longer session sticky TTL.
[00:13:29] Samira: we can increase TTL from 30s to 90s for the test route.

[00:13:40] [00:13:40] Jordan: ok we'll mark that in the runbook as recommended config change.

[00:13:55] Oliver: does Redwood support a canary rollback triggered automatically on latency regression?
[00:14:02] Priya: yes we can set an automated rollback if p95 exceeds baseline by 30% for a 10-minute window. that's part of our rollout config.

[00:14:20] [00:14:20] Alex: any other items from NexusMed?
[00:14:25] Maya: just please include the eval diff report for hallucination checks.
[00:14:30] Diego: and security wants an SSO/SAML integration plan — we have an Okta instance.
[00:14:36] Alex: ok we'll send the SSO flow; it's pretty standard SAML 2.0, we'll list the endpoints.

[00:14:50] [00:14:50] Priya: last technical note — if you want to avoid KV cold loads during AZ failover we can pre-warm a warm standby with a moving window of hot prompts; it's a small cost but it cuts p99 by ~60% in our tests.
[00:15:08] Samira: let's try warm standby for the internal inference route.

[00:15:20] Alex: great, we'll add that to the plan. I'll recap next steps and owners in an email.
[00:15:28] Oliver: thanks all.

End transcript. Artifacts shared: link: https://redwood-internal-bucket/pocs/nexusmed/2025-12-10/bench-results.csv (note: preview only), runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/poc/nexusmed/runbook-v1.md, estimator: https://sheets.redwood.ai/estimators/nexusmed-poc (view-only).

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-labels (Speaker 3/4), punctuation missing, some technical names may be mis-cased (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash, VPC -> V P C)
